m:covent: Free to walk around the streets. The shops in Covent Garden Market are among the most expensive in the city: to eat, choose Chinatown or the side streets.
m:trafalgar: The National Gallery is free: open 10am–6pm, Fridays until 9pm. For the masterpieces 60–90 minutes is enough; free booking is optional.
m:westminster: From outside it's free. The Abbey costs £32 (about €38), can't be visited on Sundays and on Saturdays closes around 1pm.
m:buckingham: The changing of the guard is on Monday, Wednesday and Friday at 11am (it can be cancelled at short notice; arrive 40 minutes early for a spot at the gates). The palace can only be visited inside at certain times of year.
m:stpaul: Inside costs £27 (about €32): open Monday to Saturday 8:30am–4:30pm (last entry 4pm), Sundays for services only. From outside you can enjoy the façade perfectly well.
m:southbank: Tate Modern is free: Sunday–Thursday 10am–6pm, Friday and Saturday 10am–9pm (last entry half an hour before). The riverside walk is always open and full of street performers.
m:borough: The market is open Tuesday to Friday 10am–5pm, Saturday 9am–5pm, Sunday 10am–4pm; closed on Mondays. For a cheap lunch, get a hot dish to share and eat on the benches by the river.
m:towerbridge: Crossing the bridge is free. The Tower Bridge Exhibition (high walkways with a glass floor and the engine rooms) costs £18 (about €21), open every day 9:30am–6pm (last entry 5pm).
m:abbeyins: Ticket £32 (about €38), best online. Open Monday to Saturday (weekdays 9:30am–3:30pm, Saturday 9am–1pm), closed to tourists on Sundays. No photos inside and modest dress required.
m:stpaulins: Ticket £27 (about €32), best online: open Monday to Saturday 8:30am–4:30pm (last entry 4pm; the dome from 9:30am), closed to visits on Sundays. No photos inside.
m:toweroflondon: Ticket £38 (about €45), best online. In October open 9am–5:30pm (Monday and Sunday from 10am), last entry 4:30pm, last guided tour at 3:15pm; from November it usually closes earlier, around 4:30pm.
m:british: Free entry to the permanent collection (booking a free entry is recommended). Open every day 10am–5pm, Fridays until 8:30pm; last entry 45 minutes before closing. Temporary exhibitions are paid separately.
m:museums: Both free. Natural History 10am–5:50pm (last entry 5:30pm); V&A 10am–5:45pm, Fridays until 10pm. If you're short of time, pick just one.
m:kensington: The parks are free, open from 5am to midnight. The palace costs £24.70 (about €29), with variable hours and opening days (usually 10am–6pm, last entry 5pm); the Queen's State Apartments are closed until spring 2027. Check the calendar on the website before buying.
m:notting: The liveliest day is Saturday, with the antiques market open all day; on other days there are fewer stalls and many shops close early.
m:camden: The markets are open every day, usually until 6pm, and very crowded at weekends. Primrose Hill is free to climb and the view is best at sunset.
m:eastend: On Sundays there's the Brick Lane market (about 10am–5pm); Old Spitalfields is also open on other days, with varying hours. The Beigel Bake bakery, open 24 hours a day, is the classic stop.
m:greenwich: The park, the market (every day about 10am–5:30pm) and the Queen's House are free; the Observatory and the Cutty Sark have tickets (check prices on the website). Get there by Thames Clipper boat (30–40 minutes from Westminster) or by DLR to Cutty Sark.
m:eye: Tickets from about £29 (€34) online, £39 (€46) at the ticket office: best to book a time slot. Open about 10am–8:30pm.
vd:regency: A historic Pimlico café with white and green tiles: full English breakfasts, toast and tea served quickly and without frills. Order at the counter and eat at the narrow tables.
vp:regency: A full breakfast with tea is generally under €12 (menu not seen).
vd:rocksole: Covent Garden's fish and chips, on a side street: fish fried in crispy batter with chips, to eat at the tables or take away. Portions are big: you can share.
vp:rocksole: A plate of fish and chips usually costs €15–20; takeaway is cheaper (menu not seen).
vd:monmouthcg: An artisan coffee roaster a short walk from Seven Dials: filter coffee and cappuccinos, freshly baked bread and pastries. Order in the queue and drink standing up or at shared tables.
vp:monmouthcg: Coffee and a pastry stay under €9 (menu not seen).
vd:bertaux: A French pâtisserie in Soho, open since 1871: éclairs, fruit tarts and croissants at the small tables upstairs, in a slightly vintage little salon.
vp:bertaux: A pastry with tea stays under €9 (menu not seen).
vd:bunhouse: Chinese steamed buns (bao) filled with pork, chicken or salted egg, in the heart of Chinatown: Soho's quick, cheap meal.
vp:bunhouse: Two or three bao with a tea are around €10–12 (menu not seen).
vd:lanzhou: Wheat noodles hand-pulled in front of you, in broth or stir-fried, in a simple room near Leicester Square; open until late.
vp:lanzhou: A bowl costs about €10–13 (menu not seen).
vd:tongue: New York-style salt beef and pastrami sandwiches, served hot in a small room in Soho. If you eat at a table it's £1 extra.
vp:tongue: A sandwich costs about €10–13 (menu not seen).
vd:leverbloom: A neighbourhood bakery with croissants, cinnamon rolls and sourdough bread, to take away: there are no tables inside.
vp:leverbloom: A croissant and a coffee stay under €8 (menu not seen).
vd:bloomscoffee: Specialty coffee a short walk from the British Museum, with pastries and toast: handy for a quiet breakfast before the museum.
vp:bloomscoffee: Coffee and a pastry stay under €9 (menu not seen).
vd:victoriahouse: A neighbourhood café and kitchen opposite the British Museum, for breakfasts and light lunches in a bright room.
vp:victoriahouse: Breakfast or a sandwich stays under €12 (menu not seen).
vd:italiauno: A Fitzrovia pizzeria and Italian kitchen, ten minutes from Tottenham Court Road: round pizza and simple pasta dishes, for a dinner that tastes of home.
vp:italiauno: A pizza costs about €12–15 (menu not seen).
vd:padella: Fresh pasta made by hand every day, in small, cheap portions, next to Borough Market. No bookings: join the queue (or the virtual list) and eat at the counter.
vp:padella: A fresh pasta dish usually costs under €15 (menu not seen).
vd:kappa: A Borough Market stall famous for its raclette cheese and onion toastie: a crispy, gooey sandwich eaten standing up. Open Thursday to Saturday only.
vd:manze: Pie and mash, a London classic for over a century: meat pie with mash and liquor (the green parsley sauce), in the tiled shop in Bermondsey.
vp:manze: Pie, mash and liquor are around €10 (menu not seen).
vd:monmouthb: The branch next to Borough Market: filter coffee, freshly baked bread and pastries. Drink standing up or at shared tables; Monmouth charges a £5 deposit for reusable cups, refunded when you bring it back.
vp:monmouthb: A coffee and a pastry stay under €9 (a latte costs about £4.20).
vd:beigel: A 24-hour bakery on Brick Lane: hot bagels with salt beef and mustard, or with salmon and cream cheese, eaten in the street.
vp:beigel: A salt beef bagel costs about €7–9 (menu not seen).
vd:pellicci: A historic family-run Italian-London café with Art Deco wooden interiors: English breakfasts, sandwiches and simple dishes in a small, noisy room.
vp:pellicci: A full breakfast under €12 (menu not seen).
vd:sipandrise: A Kensington café and bakery with croissants, bread and homemade cakes, and little tables to stop at.
vd:kenterrace: A café at the entrance to Kensington Gardens: breakfasts and sandwiches a short walk from the park and the palace.
vp:kenterrace: Breakfast or a sandwich under €12 (menu not seen).
vd:churchill: London's most photographed pub, covered in flowers outside, with a Thai restaurant in the back room: curries and noodles at pub prices. The kitchen may close before the bar: arrive early.
vp:churchill: A Thai dish usually costs €12–15 (menu not seen).
vd:truly: A café next to Camden Lock with English breakfasts, sandwiches and burgers at fair prices, open from morning to evening.
vd:fields: A vegan café in Kentish Town, with sandwiches, cakes and good coffee: fine for non-vegans too.
vp:fields: Breakfast or a sandwich under €12 (menu not seen).
vd:pedro: A neighbourhood café with breakfasts, toast and sandwiches made to order, popular with residents.
vp:pedro: Breakfast or a sandwich under €10 (menu not seen).
vd:goddards: Pie and mash in Greenwich for over a century: meat pie with mash and liquor, a short walk from the market.
vp:goddards: A plate is around €10–12 (menu not seen).
cd:shard: London's tallest skyscraper: a 360-degree view of the city from the 72nd floor.
cd:warrooms: The underground bunker where Churchill ran the war, with the rooms left as they were in 1945.
cd:tussauds: The wax museum of stars, royals and sports figures.
cd:globe: The reconstruction of Shakespeare's Elizabethan theatre, with a guided tour.
cd:kew: The great botanical garden: Victorian glasshouses, a treetop walkway and avenues to stroll.
cd:tamigi: From Westminster Pier to the Tower of London on the water, with the great monuments along the banks.
cd:belfast: A Second World War cruiser moored on the Thames, to explore from the deck to the engine room.
cd:ltmuseum: Buses, trams and carriages from the world's oldest underground, in Covent Garden.
